sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:174349
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21445 of 2024
Applicant :- Zulfiqar

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rahul Dev Singh,Sarve Nazir,Zafar Abbas
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shailesh Kumar,Subedar Mishra
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Zafar Abbas, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Shailesh Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Manav Chaurasiya, learned AGA for the State.
2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.68 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station-Bilari,
District-Moradabad during pendency of the trial.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and this is the second bail application and the first bail application has been dismissed by this Court on 12.12.2023 after considering the fact that as according to the doctor, deceased died due to the consumption of Sulfuric Acid, therefore, prima facie, it does not appear to be a case of suicidal death, but at the time of hearing of first bail application, this fact could not be brought to the notice of this Court that even by consuming sulfuric Acid, suicide can be committed.

He placed reliance in this regard upon the Modi's Medical Jurisprudence & Toxicology, 21st Edition.

sentences.text: 4. He further submits that it appears that by consuming Sulfuric Acid, deceased, i.e., wife of the applicant committed suicide on trivial matrimonial dispute.

5. He further submits that in the charge-sheet, there are as many as 33 witnesses and till date, only 8 witnesses could be examined and, therefore, trial of the case is moving with languid pace and there is no hope of its early disposal.
He next submits that in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 11.4.2022, i.e., for last more than two and a half years.

4. He further submits that however, parents of the deceased during trial supported the prosecution case, but when her sister was examined by the trial court then after cross-examination, she has been declared hostile.
5. He further submits that, therefore, considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should be released on bail.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submits that applicant is husband of the deceased and this is the second bail application and his first bail application has already been rejected after considering the entire facts of the case, but both the counsels could not dispute the fact that deceased died due to the consumption of Sulfuric Acid and as per the Modi's Medical Jurisprudence & Toxicology, 21st Edition, suicide can be committed even by consuming Sulfuric Acid.

They further could not dispute the fact that in the present matter applicant is in jail for last more than two and a half years and till date, only 8 witnesses could be examined out of total 33 witnesses.
They further could not dispute the fact that sister of the deceased after her cross-examination has been declared hostile.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. This is the second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant, who is husband of the deceased and his first bail application has been rejected by this Court after considering the fact that he is husband of the deceased and as deceased died due to the consumption of Sulfuric Acid, therefore, it does not appear to be a case of suicidal death, but from the Modi's Medical Jurisprudence &
Toxicology (21st Edition), which was produced by the learned counsel for the applicant, it reflects that even due to consumption of Sulfuric Acid, suicide can be committed.
Therefore, at this stage, it cannot be said that deceased did not commit suicide.

8. Further, in the present matter, applicant is in jail since April, 2022, i.e., for last more than two and a half years and till date out of 33 witnesses of the charge-sheet, only 8 witnesses could be examined, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of the trial.
9. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history and sister of the deceased during trial after her cross-examination has been declared hostile.

8. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Zulfiqar vs State Of U.P. on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121809491/
2 10.
Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Zulfiqar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 6.11.2024 LN Tripathi  Zulfiqar vs State Of U.P. on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121809491/
